current_answer: Current evidence supports four separate choices: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted, context-carrying WebRTC session; Reactor FastH3 has separate build and playout queues whose default output stops to black unless an optional autoplay policy advances a ready clip; FastVideo FastH3 Preview has local clip routes; and Comfy’s optimized H3 route broadens local access. No low-cost, independently proven setup delivers continuous context at viewer speed.

catalogue_card.question: Does FastH3 play the next clip by itself?
catalogue_card.text: Not by default. Reactor’s FastH3 queue goes black after a clip until a client plays the next one or enables autoplay. That can pace ready scenes, not preserve the story.

summary: Reactor documents a FastH3 queue whose default completed or stopped output flushes to black; its optional autoplay can start a ready playout-front clip when nothing is playing.
Autoplay changes playout control, not the model boundary: the project says independently generated FastH3 clips hard-cut without carried subject, framing, or voice.
fal’s current H3 Max Director page still describes the closest route to one continuing, directed session. It lists $0.02 per generated second right now and $0.08 from 14 September 2026.
A fresh 12 GB local-H3 community workflow report targets a 60-second output but gives a stated fastest Turbo time of 35 minutes 11 seconds; it is an offline lead, not a live claim.
ComfyUI v0.35.0 adds H3 features, while a fresh issue reports one failure in its experimental H3 sparse-attention path; treat a new version as a condition to test.
uncertainty: Reactor’s playout, continuity, and timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
The 12 GB longform workflow and the ComfyUI experimental-feature issue are individual community reports, not general compatibility or performance evidence.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 13 September 2026. FastH3 playout behavior, H3 local compatibility, ComfyUI versions, and fal pricing can change quickly; the stated Director price change begins 14 September 2026.
